It fails on multiple requirements: 1. **RSS 2.0 parsing is completely broken.** `parse_rss` looks for elements with fabricated namespaces such as `{http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/channel/}channel`. Standard RSS 2.0 has no namespace, so the correct tag is simply `channel`. Consequently, `parse_rss` never finds the channel and always returns `(None, None, None)` for a valid RSS feed. 2. **Unhandled `ValueError` on parse failure.** On failure, `parse_rss` and `parse_atom` return three values (`None, None, None`), but `main` attempts to unpack them into two variables: `title, items = parse_rss(feed_xml)`. This raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack`, which is not caught. The program crashes with a traceback instead of printing `error: ` and exiting with status 2. 3. **Incorrect HTML line breaks for multiple items.** The loop appends `
  • ...
    • ` without a trailing newline. For more than one item, the `
  • ` elements are concatenated on the same line (e.g., `
  • 1
  • 2
    • `), violating the requirement that there must be one `
  • ` line per item. 4. **Atom missing link outputs `None` instead of an empty string.** If no matching `link` is found, `link_entry` remains `None`, and the f-string inserts the literal string `None` into the `href` attribute. The task requires an empty string for missing links. 5. **Fragile format detection.** The code uses `'rss' in feed_xml.lower()` to detect RSS. An Atom feed that contains the substring `rss` anywhere (e.g., in a link URL) will be misclassified as RSS and fail. 6. **Zero-item feeds are treated as errors.** `if not title or not items:` causes an error exit when a valid feed has zero items. The task does not state that an empty item list is invalid; it should simply produce an empty `
